title: Ordinary henselization under a quasi-finite local map
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map of finite type, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be primes with $\mathfrak q$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, and assume $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Write $A_{\mathfrak p}^h$ and $B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ for ordinary henselizations [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then the canonical map $A_{\mathfrak p}^h\to B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ is finite and local, and $B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ is canonically the localization of $A_{\mathfrak p}^h\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\mathfrak q}$ at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$.

mathlib_searches.query: For a quasi-finite ring map at a prime, the ordinary henselization of the target is the localization of the tensor product with the ordinary henselization of the source and the map is finite
mathlib_searches.results: Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt, Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.baseChange, Algebra.QuasiFinite.finite_fiber; no ordinary henselization comparison theorem.
